ShortDescription.Value: Build one city together. Roads, zoning, terrain and policies sync live; a small server window (or a Linux server) holds the shared city.

Publish.LongDescription:
Co-op multiplayer for Cities: Skylines II built around a **server window**: a small console app that holds the shared city and relays what everyone does.
**How it works** - Main menu > **Multiplayer**. **Host game** opens the server window next to your game and joins it; friends join your address and port. **Join game** connects to a friend or to a dedicated server. - Joining fetches the shared city and loads it. Anyone can save the city to the server from the in-game panel (bottom-right button); the host also saves automatically every few minutes. - What anyone builds, zones, bulldozes, terraforms or sets in a panel (taxes, budgets, fees, policies, building options) shows up on every PC live, and everyone shares one treasury. You see where the other players are on the map. - The simulation itself runs per PC, so citizens and traffic can differ a little; a save from anyone brings the others back in line.
**Mods** Any mod is allowed as long as everyone runs the same playset. The server compares mod lists (ignoring version numbers) and tells a rejected player which playset to activate. A dedicated server can follow a published Paradox playset by itself.
**Dedicated server** The same window runs on a Linux or Windows box without the game. Downloads and setup notes are on GitHub.
Early access: play with people you know, keep regular saves, and report problems on GitHub.
Publish.ChangeLog: 0.2.6: Fixes other players' games crashing when someone places a farm, forestry, mining or oil area: those areas are no longer sent live and arrive with the next save instead. When the host connects and the server already holds a city, the game asks whether to load it or start a new world (map list opens, mod maps included). Fetching the server's city on purpose no longer re-uploads it as a new one. 0.2.5: Traffic Tool Essentials settings now follow the player who changes them (junction signals, phases, lane groups, lane directions, labels, sync groups, depot zones). New city button on the Join screen: the host starts a fresh city on any map and it replaces the one on the server. A player is told when their build could not be recreated on someone else's PC. Connections survive 30 s of silence; the server window no longer freezes when clicked; its console no longer logs every player-position update. 0.2.4: the mod's own Paradox entry no longer counts in mod-list checks (subscribers were seen as having an extra mod). Dedicated servers now read all settings from server.json and reload it live. 0.2.3: first published build. Server window, shared city, live build sync (roads, buildings, zoning, terrain, transit lines), city settings and building options sync, shared treasury, player markers on the map, anyone can save, menu screens, in-game panel, playset-aware mod check, server update check.
